purpose: Reusable, source-verified signature football sequences for Philadelphia Gamecast stars. Named celebrations are not invented; this batch encodes only moves explicitly supported by authoritative Eagles/NFL material.

productionContract.camera: three-quarter Gamecast hero angle; preserve approved Dallas camera without cuts or jumps
productionContract.lighting: shared neutral stadium key/fill/rim rig; identical approved Dallas production lighting
productionContract.anchor: bottom-center ground-contact anchor; airborne/assisted motion resolves to the same projected world anchor
productionContract.scale: reuse locked player-specific PHI base-chibi proportions; no sequence rescaling
productionContract.appearance: reuse locked current official Philadelphia Eagles headshot appearance and skin tone; never infer appearance from name
productionContract.uniform: Philadelphia current uniform geometry and current roster number remain locked across every frame

sourceAuthority.note: NFL material explicitly identifies Philadelphia's Brotherly Shove/Tush Push with Hurts as the ball carrier. This is encoded as a signature team football move centered on Hurts, not mislabeled as a player celebration.

animation.rootMotion: Gamecast supplies short-yardage forward displacement; Hurts rig preserves the bottom-center projected anchor until snap, then resolves cleanly to the post-play anchor after the compact surge

beats.direction: compact under-center stance with low hips and stable feet; preserve #1, face, proportions and ball relationship
secure the snap immediately at the torso with shoulders lowered for short-yardage leverage
drive behind the interior line with compact forward lean; avoid exaggerated horizontal launch
sell the recognizable teammate-assisted forward surge through torso compression and leg drive; teammate force is event-layered and must not distort Hurts' rig
maintain secure ball position while finishing the surge; only extend if Gamecast marks the play as a score/line-to-gain conversion
settle safely from the push with no limb intersection, scale pop or foot teleport

sourceAuthority.note: Philadelphia's official coverage quotes Smith describing sideline awareness/toe tapping as 'kind of my thing,' and later team video calls out his repeated sideline dance. The asset is therefore a verified signature receiving skill, not a named touchdown celebration.

animation.rootMotion: route locomotion supplies approach; animation controls catch, toe drag/tap and balance while the final planted foot resolves to the projected sideline/end-zone anchor

beats.direction: enter from route locomotion with lean receiver proportions and #6 locked; eyes track the event-layer ball
form a natural catch window without obscuring the face unnecessarily; secure the ball before boundary footwork
place the first foot inside the boundary with controlled ankle/knee flexion and no foot sliding
bring the second foot down into the recognizable precise toe-tap/toe-drag silhouette while maintaining possession
counterbalance upper body over the legal catch plane; keep limbs readable and avoid clipping
finish into possession/post-catch state or touchdown settle according to event result

rules: Current player identity, appearance and number remain governed by the locked 2026 PHI roster/headshot references.
A named celebration is only encoded when authoritative evidence supports that exact celebration.
A repeatable iconic football move may be encoded as a signature sequence but must not be mislabeled as a celebration.
Generic celebration fallbacks remain available and are not replaced by these event-specific signature moves.

requirements: Sequence entry/exit blends with PHI action-pose keys without camera, lighting, scale or anchor pops.
Uniform number, face, skin tone, hair/facial-hair reference and body proportions remain unchanged through every beat.
Transparent alpha edges remain clean during fast feet, hands, ball interaction and assisted motion.
Gamecast only triggers each signature when the matching play context exists.
